root_cause: The MFA UI component was replaced with a segmented 6-box OTP input where each digit has its own `<input class='mfa-otp-digit-input'>` element. Calling `MfaOtpDigits.FillAsync(sixDigitCode)` directly on the multi-element locator triggered a Playwright strict mode violation.
resolution: Updated `CompleteMfaChallengeAsync` in `LoginPage.cs` to target `MfaOtpDigits.First` and use `PressSequentiallyAsync(sixDigitCode)` (or paste event) so the component auto-advances across all 6 inputs, or iterate via `Nth(i).FillAsync()`.

error_message: Microsoft.Playwright.PlaywrightException : Inventory reservation API failed with HTTP 502: Bad Gateway
root_cause: The downstream `inventory-reservation-service` pods in the QA Kubernetes cluster restarted during an automated Helm deployment while holding open Redis distributed locks, causing NGINX ingress to return HTTP 502 Bad Gateway on `POST /api/v2/inventory/reserve`.
resolution: Configured readiness/liveness probe grace periods on `inventory-reservation-service` in QA and added exponential backoff retry policy in the API Gateway for transient 502/503 upstream errors.

root_cause: `DismissCookieBannerIfPresentAsync()` used `CookieConsentAcceptBtn.IsVisibleAsync()`, which returns `false` immediately without waiting when the third-party OneTrust script loads asynchronously 600ms after `DOMContentLoaded`. The banner then appeared right as `SignInButton.ClickAsync()` executed, intercepting pointer events.
resolution: Replaced the racy `IsVisibleAsync()` check in `LoginPage.cs` (line 38) with `await _page.AddLocatorHandlerAsync(CookieConsentAcceptBtn, async btn => await btn.ClickAsync())` so Playwright automatically dismisses the overlay whenever it blocks an action.
